app.title: From Mud to Crown
difficulty.title: Difficulty
difficulty.pick: Choose how hard life in the village will be. It can't be changed later.
difficulty.easy.desc: Better prices, lower taxes and costs, fewer mishaps and bad weather
difficulty.normal.desc: As intended: you must save for the accounts
difficulty.hard.desc: Worse prices, higher taxes and costs, more mishaps and harsh winters
menu.title: Menu
menu.confirmNew: Your current game will be lost if you haven't saved it. Start over?
menu.howTo: Tap a plot to sow and again to harvest. Tap the henhouse or cow pen to collect, and the house or granary to upgrade them (they need coins and materials from the market). Hire villagers: farmers sow and harvest by themselves, but everyone eats from your pantry. You pay taxes every season. Progress shows what each level unlocks.
menu.saveHintFile: Your game is saved to a file on your device. Once you pick it, it saves itself every few in-game days.
menu.saveHintDownload: Your game downloads as a .json file. To keep playing, load it from this menu.
market.title: Village market
market.subtitle: Prices change every week and with the season
msg.protectionActive: You already have that protection until the accounts
protection.crops.desc: Against pests and drought on your crops.
market.protectionHint: Paid now, it lasts until the next accounts. It costs more the more plots or animals you have.
seasonCard.debt: You owe your lord {n} coins. It grows 10% each season and, above {limit}, it will be taken in land.
seasonCard.seized.lease: Seizure: your lord takes a leased field to settle the debt.
seasonCard.seized.plot: Seizure: your lord takes a plot to settle the debt.
seasonCard.rankWarning: Your lord doubts you. If you still lack the favour your rank requires at the next accounts, you will lose it.
seasonCard.rankLost: You have lost the rank of {lost}: you are {rank} again. Regain favour to rise once more.
save.error.format: That file isn't a From Mud to Crown save
save.error.newer: That save comes from a newer version of the game
msg.dormant: Out of season ({crop}): it won't grow until the season changes
msg.winterNoCrops: The ground is frozen in winter: nothing can be sown
msg.landLocked: You can clear land at level {level}
msg.landLimit: Your level allows no more than {max} plots
msg.animalLocked: You can't buy that animal yet
msg.bought.chicken: A new hen in the coop
msg.bought.cow: A new cow in the pen
msg.optionUnavailable: You can't choose that right now
msg.season.winter: Winter arrives: wheat and carrots won't grow until spring
plant.title: What will you sow?
land.title: Clear a plot
land.text: Clearing and ploughing this land costs {cost} coins. Each new plot costs more than the last.
levelup.title: Level {level}
levelup.unlock.buyLand: You can clear the grass next to the field
levelup.unlock.buyChicken: You can buy hens at the market
levelup.unlock.buyCow: You can buy cows at the market
levelup.unlock.renown: Renown: from now on, every {xp} XP gives you {prestige} prestige when the season closes
event.peddler.title: The peddler
event.peddler.text: A peddler laden with bundles stops at your door. He pays well for fresh eggs and carries a laying hen in a wicker cage.
event.peddler.result.sellEggs: He takes {amount} eggs and leaves you {coins} coins.
event.peddler.result.buyHen: The hen settles into the coop as if she had always lived there.
event.peddler.result.decline: The peddler shrugs and goes on his way.
event.fair.title: Fair in town
event.fair.text: Minstrels and merchants have come from afar. For a few days market prices will soar.
event.fair.result.go: The town is bustling: make the most of it and sell these days.
event.fair.result.decline: Another time. The farm doesn't tend itself.
event.smith.title: The travelling smith
event.smith.text: A smith carrying his anvil looks for a place to stay a few nights. For bed and board he would forge you tools for less.
event.smith.result.host: For 10 days tools will cost you 30% less.
event.smith.result.decline: The smith moves on towards town.
event.feast.title: Feast at the castle
event.feast.text: The baron's steward needs milk for tonight's feast and pays double. The baron will like to know who served him.
event.feast.result.sellMilk: You sell {amount} milk for {coins} coins. The baron takes note.
event.pilgrims.title: Pilgrims
event.pilgrims.text: A band of pilgrims bound for the shrine asks for wheat. They can pay something, or you can give it as charity and the village will hear of it.
event.pilgrims.result.sell: They take {amount} wheat and pay you {coins} coins.
event.pilgrims.result.give: The pilgrims bless you. The village speaks well of you.
event.pilgrims.result.decline: The pilgrims continue on their way.
event.monk.title: The abbey monk
event.monk.text: A monk offers blessed seed from the abbey for alms. It will last for several sowings.
event.monk.result.buy: Your next 4 sowings will be free.
event.monk.result.decline: The monk smiles and continues his round.
event.wedding.title: A village wedding
event.wedding.text: One of your villagers is getting married. The bride needs a home and work, and the whole village is invited to the feast.
event.wedding.result.welcome: One more villager joins the farm.
event.wedding.result.gift: The couple thank you for the gift in front of the whole village.
event.wedding.result.decline: You dance a while and go back to work.
event.farmhand.title: A farmhand seeks work
event.farmhand.text: A sturdy young man knocks at your door. He'll work the land for bed and board.
event.farmhand.result.hire: You have one more villager. Remember: he eats from your harvest every day.
event.farmhand.result.decline: He leaves to try his luck in town.
event.levy.title: The baron's levy
event.levy.text: The baron's men demand wheat for the war. You can hand it over, pay in coin or refuse — but the baron does not forget.
event.levy.result.give: The baron is grateful for your loyalty.
event.levy.result.pay: The collector counts the coins and leaves without a word.
event.levy.result.refuse: The baron is angry: next season you'll pay 50% more tribute.
event.corvee.title: Labour for the baron
event.corvee.text: The baron demands hands to repair the castle wall. Your villagers would leave the farm for a few days.
event.corvee.result.send: Your villagers will work for the baron for 3 days.
event.corvee.result.pay: You pay and your villagers stay on the farm.
event.corvee.result.refuse: The baron will raise your tribute by 25% next season.
event.chapel.title: The village chapel
event.chapel.text: The chapel roof is falling apart. The priest asks every family to help as they can.
event.chapel.result.coins: The priest mentions your name at Sunday mass.
event.chapel.result.wheat: The priest is grateful for the wheat for the workers.
event.chapel.result.refuse: The village mutters about your meanness.
event.road.title: The road to town
event.road.text: The rains have wrecked the road to market. The neighbours are getting together to fix it.
event.road.result.work: Your villagers spend 2 days on the road. The neighbours are grateful.
event.road.result.pay: The stonemason leaves the road like new.
event.road.result.refuse: The road stays broken: for 14 days you'll sell everything 10% cheaper.
event.hunt.title: The baron's hunt
event.hunt.text: The baron is out hunting and his huntsmen expect the local farms to feed them.
event.hunt.result.provide: The huntsmen eat well and tell the baron so.
event.hunt.result.pay: The huntsmen take the coins and move on to another farm.
event.hunt.result.refuse: The baron will raise your tribute by 20% next season.
event.baronsMen.title: The baron's men
event.baronsMen.text: The baron's soldiers are back: they haven't forgotten you refused the levy. They want the debt settled.
event.baronsMen.result.pay: Debt settled. The baron considers the matter closed.
event.baronsMen.result.hide: They find nothing and leave empty-handed.
event.baronsMen.result.hide.fail: They find the hiding place and take {lost} of your harvest.
event.fox.title: A fox prowls the coop
event.fox.text: Last night you heard the hens in a flurry. There are fox tracks by the fence.
event.fox.result.fence: The fence holds. The fox will have to look elsewhere.
event.fox.result.risk: The fox hasn't come back. For now.
event.fox.result.risk.fail: The fox took a hen. It knows where to come back.
event.foxDen.title: The den
event.foxDen.text: The fox has been prowling again. A neighbour has found its den in the woods.
event.foxDen.result.trapper: The trapper deals with the fox. The village breathes easy.
event.foxDen.result.hunt: You find the fox and drive it off for good.
event.foxDen.result.hunt.fail: The fox flees, but takes another hen first. It won't be back.
event.pests.title: Pests in the field
event.pests.text: Little black bugs are eating the shoots. A neighbour swears herb smoke drives them off.
event.pests.result.smoke: The smoke drives the pests away.
event.pests.result.risk: The pests leave on their own.
event.pests.result.risk.fail: The pests set all your crops back 2 days.
event.storm.title: A storm is coming
event.storm.text: Black clouds over the hills. The granary roof won't hold for long.
event.storm.result.shelter: Your villagers spend the day covering the granary. All safe.
event.storm.result.risk.fail: Water gets into the granary: you lose {lost} of your harvest.
event.sickCow.title: The cow is sick
event.sickCow.text: The cow won't eat and barely gives milk. The village herbwife knows about such things.
event.sickCow.result.herbalist: With her herbs, the cow recovers at once.
event.sickCow.result.risk: The cow recovers on her own.
event.sickCow.result.risk.fail: The sickness spreads: your animals will give half for 10 days.
event.thieves.title: Thieves on the road
event.thieves.text: Word in the village is that a band of thieves is prowling the farms at night.
event.thieves.result.watch: The watchman stays up all night. Nothing to fear.
event.thieves.result.risk.fail: They broke into the granary: {lost} of your stores are gone.
event.drought.title: Drought
event.drought.text: It hasn't rained for weeks and the well is low. The crops are turning yellow.
event.drought.result.carry: Your villagers spend 3 days hauling buckets. The crops are saved.
event.drought.result.risk.fail: Without rain, crops will grow at half speed for 7 days.

msg.buildingMaxed: This building can't be upgraded any further
msg.noFreeBed: No free beds: upgrade the house
msg.villagersHungry: Your villagers are hungry: the granary has no food left
msg.villagerLeftHunger: {name} has left: there was nothing to eat
msg.carterSold: The carter sold {amount} goods for {coins} coins
msg.wildLocked: The baron's lands. They'll open when you're a Landowner
msg.leased: Plot leased (−{cost} coins). Rent: {rent} per season
msg.tenant: A tenant works this land: he pays you {rent} coins each season
rank.peasant.desc: You work your own land, but you have next to nothing.
rank.freeFarmer.desc: You owe nobody anything. You can buy cows at the market.
rank.landowner.desc: The baron recognises you. The eastern lands open up to lease to tenants.
building.house.desc: Your villagers sleep here. Every bed is one more mouth to feed.
building.granary.desc: Everything you harvest and collect is stored here. Once it's full, nothing more fits.
building.coop.desc: Hens lay an egg a day. More room, more hens.
building.pen.desc: The cow gives milk every two days. A good pen gives more milk.
villagers.noBed: Upgrade the house for more beds
villagers.food: Food for {days} days · they eat {perDay} a day
villagers.empty: You have no villagers yet. They need a bed and eat from your harvest every day, but they work for you.
job.farmer.title: Farmer
job.herder.title: Herder
job.carter.title: Carter
job.farmer.desc: Sows and harvests their plots and makes everything grow {n}% faster
job.herder.desc: +{n}% eggs and milk, and collects them for you
job.carter.desc: Every {days} days sells the surplus at {rate}% of the price
progress.title: Progress
progress.start: You start with your house, the field, four hens and a cow
progress.where.field: tap the grass by the field
progress.toolsIntro: Each villager carries their own tool. Upgrading it multiplies what they add to their job.
estate.king.desc: Rises by serving in the host and the jousts, and with the charter of nobility. Collects the tolls on the royal roads.
estate.nobles.desc: Your lord and his peers. Rises by meeting their demands and paying tribute. Decides how much tribute you pay.
estate.artisans.desc: Guilds and merchants. Rises with workshops, their upgrades and fair orders. Sets the price of materials.
estate.commoners.desc: Your neighbours and villagers. Rises by helping them and paying wages. Decides wages and the cost of hiring.
estate.church.desc: The abbey and the bishop. Rises with donations, paid tithes and the chapel. Decides the tithe.
progress.estatesHint: What pleases one estate displeases its rival a little, and with each accounts relations slowly drift back towards 50 unless you tend them.
progress.taxesText: At the start of each season you pay the tithe ({tithe}% of market earnings) and the {liege}'s tribute ({base} + {perPlot} per plot).
seasonCard.title: {season} accounts
seasonCard.unpaid: You couldn't pay {n} coins: the {liege} is displeased.
rankCard.title: New rank!
lease.title: Lease a plot
lease.text: A tenant will work this land and pay you {rent} coins each season. It counts as a plot for tribute.
seasonCard.grace: The baron takes no taxes in your first season. From now on, you pay every season.
market.materialsHint: Building upgrades and tools need materials as well as coins. They're kept in a separate store and don't take granary space.
farmer.noPlots: No plots left: clear more land
farmer.outOfSeason: {crop} is out of season: their plots wait
pantry.intro: Choose what villagers may eat. They eat the cheapest first, and what you keep in reserve won't be sold by accident.
pantry.needs: They eat {perDay} a day · food for {days} days
pantry.noVillagers: You have no villagers to feed yet
pantry.reserveHint: Days of food to keep: the market warns you before selling it and the carter leaves it alone.
market.allReserved: All of it is reserved as food: move the slider if you still want to sell
job.artisan.title: Artisan
job.artisan.desc: Works in a workshop turning granary goods into something better
rank.artisan.desc: The guild recognises you: what your workshops make sells 15% dearer, and their best upgrades open up.
workshop.bakery.desc: Makes bread from flour and eggs: it sells well and villagers eat it.
workshop.cheesery.desc: Cures milk into cheese, the dearest goods in town.
workshop.status.noInputs: Idle: missing ingredients (the pantry reserve is left alone)
workshop.noArtisan: Nobody works here. Assign one of your villagers: they'll leave their job and become an artisan.
workshop.notBuilt: From level {level} · {cost} coins, on a building plot
site.title: Building plot
site.text: A good spot for a workshop. Each workshop can be built only once.
artisan.noWorkshops: No workshops yet: build them on the plots on the map
progress.branchesHint: Branch titles add to your rank: you can hold several.
progress.where.site: tap a building plot on the map
progress.workshopsHint: They're built on the map's plots and need an artisan.
event.bakerOrder.title: An order from the castle
event.bakerOrder.text: The baron's steward needs bread for the garrison and pays well above market price.
event.bakerOrder.result.sell: He takes {amount} loaves and pays you {coins} coins. The baron is pleased.
event.bakerOrder.result.decline: The steward buys his bread in town.
event.cheeseFair.title: Cheese fair
event.cheeseFair.text: Merchants from neighbouring towns arrive looking for good cured cheese.
event.rats.title: Rats in the mill
event.rats.text: There are droppings between the sacks and something gnawed the flour last night.
event.rats.result.cat: The cat struts round the mill like a lord. Not a rat in sight.
event.rats.result.risk.fail: The rats eat {lost} of your wheat and flour.
hud.caravans: {n} caravans on the road · the first returns in {days} days
trade.locked: Trade with other towns opens at level {level}.
trade.intro: Load a cart with your surplus and send it to another town: they pay more for what they lack. The price is fixed when it leaves.
trade.cartsInfo: {n} of {max} · {free} free · holds {cap} · {upkeep} per season each
trade.stallInfo: You sell without middlemen: {n}% more at the home market.
trade.stallOwned: You have your own stall: you sell 10% dearer.
trade.allOut: All carts are on the road.
trade.escortHint: Without escort, a {risk}% chance of bandits: half the sale is lost.
trade.problem.coins: You need {cost} coins to set off
trade.back.ok: The caravan from {town} is back: +{coins} coins
trade.back.robbed: The caravan from {town} was robbed: +{coins} coins
trade.back.okText: The carter arrives with a full purse and good news from the road.
trade.back.robbedText: Bandits attacked the cart on the road. The carter saved what he could.
msg.stallBought: You now own a market stall (−{cost} coins)
msg.caravanSent: The caravan leaves for {town} with {units} units: back in {days} days
progress.unlock.trade: Trade with other towns: your first cart
rank.burgher.desc: Merchants treat you as one of their own: bigger carts, half tolls and better prices in other towns.
event.ironPeddler.title: A peddler with iron
event.ironPeddler.text: A peddler from the mines brings iron bars and sells them cheaper than the market.
event.ironPeddler.result.buy: You store the bars in the shed.
event.ironPeddler.result.decline: The peddler goes on his way.
event.bridgeOut.title: Bridge down
event.bridgeOut.text: The flood has washed away the bridge on the king's road. Your caravans will have to wait, or someone must pay for repairs.
event.bridgeOut.result.repair: The bridge is ready in a day. The village appreciates it.
event.bridgeOut.result.wait: Your caravans will take 2 more days to return.
rank.lord.desc: The king has sold you a patent of nobility. Your fief opens to the south: raise the manor, take the hamlets and gather your retinue.
rank.baron.desc: The old baron cedes you his barony. You no longer answer to him but to the count, who does not know you yet.
rank.count.desc: The king names you count. Only the Crown stands above you now.
progress.req.branches: A branch title: Artisan or Burgher
progress.nobilityHint: Once you meet everything else, the king sells you a patent of nobility and you become Lord. Baron and Count are earned through your fief.
progress.unlock.charter: Patent of nobility, if you meet the rest
noble.charterReady: The king is willing to sell you a patent of nobility.
noble.charterNotReady: The king will not sell you the patent yet: you are missing something.
noble.notNoble: You must be a Lord first.
msg.charterReady: The king is willing to sell you a patent of nobility. See Progress › Ranks.
msg.charterBought: Patent of nobility bought for {cost} coins.
noble.title: Your fief
noble.sub: Manor, vassal hamlets, retinue and patronage.
noble.prestigeHint: Prestige comes from works, hamlets, patronage and feats. Baron and Count require it.
noble.houseIntro: Each work grants prestige and more: room for soldiers, a chapel that lowers the tithe, a great hall that brings fame every season.
manorUp.hall.desc: A stone house worthy of your name.
manorUp.wall.desc: A crenellated enclosure around the house.
manorUp.chapel.desc: Mass at home: the tithe stays in the family.
manorUp.keep.desc: A tower seen from all across the valley.
manorUp.greatHall.desc: Where feasts are held and envoys received.
hamlet.woodcutters.desc: A woodcutters' hamlet in the oak wood.
hamlet.quarry.desc: A stonecutters' hamlet below the crags.
hamlet.mine.desc: A mining hamlet at the mouth of an old mine.
noble.fiefIntro: Hamlets pay you dues and deliver their material every season. The more the village likes you, the more they pay.
noble.hostIntro: Paid soldiers: each earns {upkeep} coins per season and leaves if unpaid. With {escort} or more, your caravans get a free escort.
noble.noRoom: The manor has no room for more soldiers: improve it.
noble.escortNeed: With {n} soldiers, caravans get a free escort.
noble.hostUses: They serve in the king's host, against bandits and in tourneys.
msg.noSoldierRoom: No room for more soldiers: improve the manor.
noble.patronageIntro: Each action can be done once per season. They turn coins into prestige and favour.
patronage.donation.desc: The monks will pray for your house.
patronage.banquet.desc: Bread, cheese and wine for the nobles of the shire.
noble.patronage.banquet.done: The banquet is the talk of the shire: +{prestige} prestige.
patronage.tourney.desc: Jousts with your soldiers before your liege and the nobility.
noble.patronage.tourney.done: The tourney crowns your house in glory: +{prestige} prestige.
seasonCard.wagesLeft: There wasn't enough to pay everyone, and they left unpaid: {names}.
seasonCard.neglected: No money for upkeep: crops and animals yield {pct}% for a season.
event.royalHost.title: The King's host
event.royalHost.text: The king summons his vassals to war. You are expected to come with your men or pay scutage.
event.royalHost.result.send: Your men return covered in glory.
event.royalHost.result.send.fail: They return in glory, but one does not come back.
event.royalHost.result.scutage: You pay and the king is satisfied.
event.royalHost.result.refuse: Your liege will not forget your absence: tribute rises 50% next season.
event.bandits.title: Bandits in the hamlets
event.bandits.text: A band of brigands is raiding the roads of your hamlets.
event.bandits.result.fight: The bandits flee and the hamlets cheer you.
event.bandits.result.fight.fail: You drive them off, but one of your soldiers falls.
event.bandits.result.endure: They take wood, stone and iron, and the hamlets grumble.
event.bishop.title: The bishop's visit
event.bishop.text: The bishop passes through your fief and expects a gift for the cathedral.
event.bishop.result.donate: The bishop blesses your house from the pulpit.
event.bishop.result.decline: The bishop goes on his way.
event.marriage.title: An advantageous match
event.marriage.text: A noble house offers its heiress to your eldest son, for a handsome dowry.
event.marriage.result.dowry: The marriage joins your house to an ancient line.
event.joust.title: Jousts at court
event.joust.text: Jousts are held at court and one of your soldiers may enter the lists.
event.joust.result.enter: He wins the joust! He brings 1500 coins and fame.
event.joust.result.enter.fail: He falls in the lists: you lose the soldier and the prize.
event.joust.result.decline: You watch the jousts from the stands.
tutorial.welcome.title: Welcome to your farm
tutorial.welcome.text: You have a house, a plot, a cow and some hens. I will show you the basics in a few steps. Time is paused while you read: the pause and play buttons stop and start it, and two or three arrows make it go faster.
tutorial.sow.title: Sow wheat
tutorial.sow.text: Tap the glowing ploughed soil to sow. Seed costs a few coins.
tutorial.collect.title: Collect the eggs
tutorial.collect.text: Hens lay every few days. When the shield with a number appears above the coop, tap it.
tutorial.harvest.title: Harvest
tutorial.harvest.text: When the wheat is ripe its plot will glow: tap it to harvest. If it takes a while, speed up with the two-arrow button.
tutorial.sell.title: Sell at the market
tutorial.sell.text: Open the Market and sell some wheat or eggs with the slider. What you keep back as food is not sold.
tutorial.progress.title: See what lies ahead
tutorial.progress.text: Harvesting, collecting and selling give experience. Open Progress to see what each level brings.
tutorial.end.title: You know the basics
tutorial.end.text: From now on, when something new arrives I will leave you a short tip. You can replay the tutorial or turn tips off from the menu.
tip.buildings.title: Improve your buildings
tip.buildings.text: Tap the house, granary, coop or pen to see their upgrades. They cost coins and materials (wood, stone, iron), bought in the market's Buy tab or straight from the panel.
tip.land.title: Break new ground
tip.land.text: You can now buy land: the grass next to your plots shows a dotted outline. Tap it to plough it. Each new plot costs a little more.
tip.villagers.title: Hire villagers
tip.villagers.text: Your house now has a free bed. In the house, Villagers tab, hire someone and give them a trade: the farmer sows and harvests alone, the herder collects from the animals and the carter sells the surplus.
tip.pantry.title: The pantry
tip.pantry.text: Villagers eat every day. In the granary, Pantry tab, choose what they may eat and how many days of food are kept unsold. If they go hungry, they leave.
tip.animals.title: More animals
tip.animals.text: In the market's Buy tab you can now buy hens (and cows soon). The coop and pen set how many fit.
tip.events.title: Decisions
tip.events.text: Every so often someone arrives with an offer, an obligation or a mishap. Offers can be turned down freely; obligations, less so.
tip.taxes.title: Taxes
tip.taxes.text: At the start of each season you pay the tithe, the baron's tribute, your villagers' wages and the upkeep of what you have built. Save for the accounts: what you don't pay angers the baron, unpaid villagers leave and what isn't kept up yields less.
tip.estates.title: The estates
tip.estates.text: The King, the Nobility, the Artisans, the Commoners and the Church remember what you do. How you stand with each changes your tribute, tithe, tolls, materials and wages. What pleases one displeases its rival: see Progress › Ranks.
tip.landowner.title: The eastern lands
tip.landowner.text: As Landowner you can lease the eastern lands to tenants: tap them to lease and they will pay rent every season.
tip.workshops.title: Workshops
tip.workshops.text: You can now raise a mill on one of the map's building sites (the staked plots). Each workshop needs an artisan villager and turns your surplus into pricier goods.
tip.trade.title: Trade
tip.trade.text: In the market's Trade tab you can buy a cart and send caravans to other towns, which pay more for what they lack. Without an escort, beware of bandits.
tip.charter.title: The patent of nobility
tip.charter.text: The king is willing to sell you a patent of nobility. Find it in Progress › Ranks: with it you become Lord and your fief opens.
tip.fief.title: Your fief
tip.fief.text: Your fief lies to the south of the map. Tap the manor to raise it, take the hamlets, recruit your retinue and earn prestige through patronage.
hud.ledger: Season accounts in {days} days: {n} coins will be charged and you have {coins}.
hud.ledgerGrace: Season accounts in {days} days: nothing is charged this time.
hud.ledgerFood: Food won't last: there is enough for {days} days.
ledger.title: Season report
ledger.when: Accounts are due in {days} days. This is what would be charged if they were today.
ledger.grace: This is the grace season: your lord charges nothing at these accounts. From the next one on, he will.
ledger.titheNote: The tithe is {pct} % of what you earn at the market this season ({earned} so far): it grows every time you sell.
ledger.ok: You can pay: after the accounts you will have {n} coins left.
ledger.risk.taxes: {n} coins of taxes would become debt with the {liege}, growing 10 % each season, and the Nobility would think less of you.
ledger.risk.neglect: There would be nothing for upkeep: crops and animals would yield less all next season.
ledger.foodNone: There are no villagers to feed.
ledger.foodOk: It lasts until the accounts ({n} rations needed).
ledger.foodShort: It won't last until the accounts: {n} rations short. Without food, after {hunger} hungry days one villager leaves each day.
ledger.tip: Keep the accounts money aside before buying or building. Food reserved in the granary pantry is never sold.
msg.ledgerShort: Accounts in {days} days: {total} coins will be charged and you are {short} short. Tap the accounts pill to see what would happen.
msg.foodLow: Food left for only {days} days: harvest, buy or reserve more in the pantry.
character.title: Your character
character.name: Your name
character.traitsHint: Your origin, your nature and your ambition. ▲ are advantages and ▼ drawbacks; they already count in everything you do.
character.noTraits: This game started before traits existed, so your character has no origin traits. Start a new game to go through the questionnaire.
trait.peasantBorn.desc: You grew up in the mud, like those who now work for you. The people see you as one of their own; the nobles, as an upstart.
trait.craftBorn.desc: You learned the trade in your father's workshop: you know the guilds and how to buy materials.
trait.nobleBastard.desc: You carry noble blood without the name. Nobles treat you better than most; the people and the Church, worse.
trait.cloisterRaised.desc: The monks taught you letters and sums. You learn fast, but you haggle little.
trait.pious.desc: You pray, fast and give alms. The Church notices, and you sell a little cheaper to your own.
trait.generous.desc: Nobody leaves your table hungry. The people love you, and your purse feels it in wages.
trait.greedy.desc: Every coin counts: you pay little and sell dear. That doesn't make friends.
trait.diligent.desc: You rise before the rooster. Your lands yield more, though so much work means more eating.
trait.shrewd.desc: You know how to close a deal and dodge a toll. Priests and common folk trust you little.
trait.crown.desc: You want a title from the king. You gain more favour with the King and the Nobility; the people find you distant.
trait.faith.desc: You want to raise a great church. The Church opens its doors to you; the guilds, less so.
trait.craft.desc: You want to be master of a guild. Craftsmen follow you; the Nobility looks down on you.
trait.trade.desc: You want a free town with its own exchange. You pay fewer tolls and sell a little dearer; the Church distrusts profit.
trait.people.desc: You want the people to choose you as their leader. More favour with the Commoners, less with the Nobility.
